record.context_brief: hyperbolic affine spheres asymptotic to cones
record.original_question: Given any convex cone, does there exist a hyperbolic affine sphere asymptotic to that cone?

evidence.quote: Question 2.5. Given any convex cone, prove the existence of a hyperbolic affine sphere which is asymptotic to this cone.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $f: M^n \to \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ be a smooth, locally strongly convex hypersurface. There is a canonical transversal vector field $\xi$ on $M$, called the affine normal, determined (up to sign) by the requirements of equiaffine differential geometry (using the Blaschke metric induced by the second fundamental form normalized by the affine invariant). The hypersurface is called an affine sphere if all affine normals either pass through a single point (the center) or are mutually parallel. An affine sphere is called hyperbolic if the affine normals all point away from a common center on the concave side of the hypersurface; equivalently, after a suitable affine change of coordinates, $M$ can be written locally as the graph of a strongly convex function $u$ on a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ satisfying the Monge–Ampère equation
$$\det(\partial_i \partial_j u) = \left(-\frac{1}{u}\right)^{n+2},$$
with $u < 0$ in $\Omega$ and $u = 0$ on $\partial \Omega$.

A convex cone $C \subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is a nonempty open convex subset such that $\lambda x \in C$ for every $x \in C$ and every $\lambda > 0$, and which contains no entire line. A complete hyperbolic affine sphere $M$ is said to be asymptotic to the cone $C$ if $M$ is contained in $C$, is properly embedded, and the closure of $M$ in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ has boundary equal to $\partial C \cup \{0\}$.

Problem. Prove that for every convex cone $C \subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ (with vertex at the origin and containing no line), and every prescribed negative constant value of the affine mean curvature, there exists a complete hyperbolic affine sphere asymptotic to $C$ with that affine mean curvature.
artifact.status_search_result: Calabi's conjecture on the existence (and uniqueness) of a complete hyperbolic affine hypersphere asymptotic to any given non-degenerate convex cone was resolved by Cheng and Yau via their work on the real Monge–Ampère equation, with later refinements/alternative proofs by Li, Gigena, and others. The statement is now an established theorem.

status_evidence.title: Cheng and Yau's work on the Monge-Ampère equation and affine geometry (Loftin survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Cheng and Yau proved that hyperbolic affine spheres are asymptotic to convex cones, and conversely that every convex cone corresponds in such a way to some hyperbolic affine sphere.
status_evidence.claim: Cheng–Yau established existence of a hyperbolic affine sphere asymptotic to any (non-degenerate) convex cone.

status_evidence.title: Calabi conjecture on hyperbolic affine hyperspheres (Math. Z.)
status_evidence.snippet: Paper devoted to the Calabi conjecture on hyperbolic affine hyperspheres asymptotic to convex cones.
status_evidence.claim: The Calabi conjecture on hyperbolic affine hyperspheres asymptotic to cones has been treated and resolved in the literature.
